printer.methodGuide.title: How printers connect to POS
printer.methodGuide.desc: Pick the method that matches your hardware. You can mix methods — each Workstation and each Kitchen Station picks its own method below. The guide here is reference; the actual choice happens on each printer card.
printer.methodGuide.matrixRow1Why: Silent + auto-print to LAN printers. One-time cert install per device.
printer.methodGuide.matrixRow2Env: Windows POS + USB cashier printer (small shop, no kitchen printers)
printer.methodGuide.matrixRow2Why: Browser = simplest (OS default printer). QZ Tray if you need silent / auto-print.
printer.methodGuide.matrixRow3Env: Android tablet POS + USB OTG / Bluetooth printer
printer.methodGuide.matrixRow3Why: QZ Tray does not run on Android. RawBT is silent + router-independent — best for emergency.
printer.methodGuide.matrixRow4Why: AirPrint via OS print dialog. QZ Tray / RawBT not available on iOS.
printer.methodGuide.matrixRow5Env: Mixed shop (Windows counter + Android kitchen tablet)
printer.methodGuide.matrixRow5Why: Each workstation / station card picks its own method. Windows → QZ Tray, Android → RawBT, anything else → Browser.
printer.methodGuide.browserDesc: Browser Print uses the OS print dialog. Every POS device supports it out of the box — no driver, no app. Best for shops that print receipts manually and don't need silent / auto-print.
printer.methodGuide.browserStep1: On each Workstation / Kitchen card below, set Connection Method = Browser Print.
printer.methodGuide.browserStep2: When a receipt prints, your OS print dialog opens — pick the printer once, then it remembers.
printer.methodGuide.browserStep3: For silent / auto-print, switch to QZ Tray (desktop) or RawBT (Android).
printer.methodGuide.rawbtDesc: RawBT is an Android-only print bridge. It silently sends prints to USB, Bluetooth, or LAN thermal printers from any Android POS / kitchen tablet. Best for mobile / handheld POS setups.
printer.methodGuide.rawbtStep1: Install RawBT from Google Play (search "RawBT print service").
printer.methodGuide.rawbtStep2: Open RawBT → Settings → Connection: pick USB / Bluetooth / Network and pair the printer.
printer.methodGuide.rawbtStep3: Open RawBT → Settings → Print: enable "Default print service".
printer.methodGuide.rawbtStep4: On each Workstation / Kitchen card below, set Connection Method = RawBT.
printer.methodGuide.rawbtStep5: Send a test print — it goes silently to the paired printer.
printer.methodGuide.rawbtNote: Note: RawBT is ignored on non-Android devices. Mix freely — Android tablets use RawBT, desktop POS uses QZ Tray, others use Browser Print.
printer.methodGuide.qzDesc: QZ Tray runs on each Windows / macOS / Linux POS device and prints silently to LAN / USB printers. Best for desktop POS counters and kitchen ticket printers — no print dialog, no per-print permission prompt after the one-time certificate install.
printer.methodGuide.qzStatusConnected: Connected to QZ Tray on this device
printer.methodGuide.qzStatusDisconnected: Not connected — click Test QZ Tray Connection above
printer.methodGuide.qzCertTitle: One-time certificate install (per device) — eliminates the "Allow print?" prompt:
printer.methodGuide.qzCertStep2: Move it into the QZ Tray data folder:
printer.methodGuide.qzCertStep3: Right-click QZ Tray tray icon → Exit, then relaunch QZ Tray.
printer.methodGuide.qzAutoInstallDesc: Download the installer for your operating system, double-click it, and the certificate is placed in the right folder automatically. No file paths to find, no hidden folders.
printer.methodGuide.qzAutoInstallAfter: After running the installer, right-click the QZ Tray tray icon → Exit, then launch QZ Tray again. Done.
printer.emergency.titleOn: Emergency Mode — ALL ORDERS ROUTED TO CASHIER
printer.emergency.descOff: One-click escape hatch for kitchen printer or network failures. Activating reroutes every order ticket to the cashier (bill) printer. Original station routing is preserved — turning OFF restores it instantly. No manual reconfiguration.
printer.emergency.descOn: Every order ticket is currently printing from the cashier (bill) printer regardless of station mapping. Staff must hand-deliver tickets to each station. Click "Turn OFF" once your kitchen printers / network are back to normal.
printer.emergency.modalOnMessage:
All order tickets will print from the cashier (bill) printer. Staff must hand-deliver tickets to each station.

If internet is down, connect this POS to a mobile hotspot. Old PCs without Wi-Fi: use a USB Wi-Fi dongle (TP-Link Nano / Mercusys / ASUS USB Adapter). Hotspot is for internet only — keep kitchen printers OFF the hotspot.
printer.emergency.modalOffMessage: Original printer routing restored. Each station prints to its own printer again.
printer.emergency.prereqTitle: Recommended cashier printer setup (for emergency mode to actually help)
printer.emergency.prereqLine1: Connect the cashier (bill) printer directly to the POS via USB or Bluetooth, NOT via the Wi-Fi router. If your LAN/router dies, a LAN cashier printer dies with it.
printer.emergency.prereqLine2: Windows POS: set the cashier card Connection Method = Browser Print (using the OS default printer set to your USB cashier printer) OR QZ Tray with the USB printer name.
printer.emergency.prereqLine3: Android POS: set the cashier card Connection Method = RawBT, pair the printer via USB OTG or Bluetooth. Router-independent — best for emergencies.
printer.emergency.prereqLine4: Kitchen printers can stay on LAN as normal — they only need to work when the network is OK. The point of this mode is that cashier alone keeps the shop running when kitchen / network is down.
printer.emergency.howItWorksTitle: How emergency mode works + recommended cashier setup
printer.emergency.coreIdea: Core idea: emergency mode just redirects EVERY ticket to the cashier printer. So how reliable it is depends entirely on how the cashier printer is connected.
printer.emergency.coreRecommendation: 👉 Recommended: connect the cashier printer directly via USB or Bluetooth (router-independent). Keep kitchen printers on LAN as normal. This way, even if the router or kitchen printers die, the cashier alone keeps the shop running.
printer.emergency.row1Behaviour: OS print dialog opens for EVERY ticket — staff must press Enter each time. No silent / auto-print.
printer.emergency.row1Ready: △ Works but slow. Switch cashier to QZ Tray / RawBT for true emergency speed.
printer.emergency.row2Behaviour: Silent auto-print. Router / Wi-Fi state does not matter — USB is independent.
printer.emergency.row3Behaviour: Silent auto-print IF the LAN is alive. If the router itself died, the cashier printer dies with it.
printer.emergency.row3Ready: ⚠ Partial — only kitchen-printer failures, not network failures.
printer.emergency.effectNote: Emergency mode changes ROUTING (all tickets → cashier), not the connection method. The cashier printer keeps using whatever method is set on its workstation card. Plan the cashier method for the worst case (USB / Bluetooth direct).
printer.emergency.preflightHeader: 🔍 Your current setup — what will happen if you turn ON
printer.emergency.routingNormal: Each station → its own printer (bar / kitchen / dessert separate)
printer.troubleshoot.title: Printer Troubleshooting Guide
printer.troubleshoot.s1Title: Permission prompt keeps appearing / "don't ask again" checkbox is greyed out
printer.troubleshoot.s1Why: QZ Tray cached a previous denial. Even with a fresh certificate, the old denial wins. Clear the cache and start over once.
printer.troubleshoot.s1Step1: QZ Tray tray icon → Tools → Manage Sites → Remove every PurpleHere / dev.purplehere.com / purplehere.com entry
printer.troubleshoot.s1Step2: QZ Tray tray icon → Exit (fully quit)
printer.troubleshoot.s1Step4: QZ Tray tab → "One-click installer (.bat)" → double-click → wait for "Certificate installed" → press a key to close
printer.troubleshoot.s1Step5: Start menu → launch QZ Tray again
printer.troubleshoot.s1Step6: QZ Tray tab → "Test QZ Tray Connection" → in the prompt, tick "remember" + Allow → done
printer.troubleshoot.s2Title: Kitchen printer doesn't print (cashier prints fine)
printer.troubleshoot.s2Why: Likely a kitchen printer power / connection / IP issue. Turn Emergency Mode ON to keep the shop running while you fix it — every ticket prints from the cashier printer.
printer.troubleshoot.s2Step1: Check kitchen printer power and paper roll
printer.troubleshoot.s2Step2: From the POS PC, open Command Prompt → "ping 192.168.x.x" (kitchen printer IP) → expect replies
printer.troubleshoot.s2Step3: Settings → Printer → Kitchen Printer card → "Test" button
printer.troubleshoot.s2Step4: Still no print → turn Emergency Mode ON → print to cashier → diagnose after closing hours
printer.troubleshoot.s3Title: Internet is down or the router crashed
printer.troubleshoot.s3Why: If your cashier printer is USB / Bluetooth direct, Emergency Mode ON keeps the shop running. LAN-only shops need a hotspot.
printer.troubleshoot.s3Step1: Tether the POS to a phone hotspot (for PurpleHere API calls)
printer.troubleshoot.s3Step2: Old PC without Wi-Fi: plug in a USB Wi-Fi dongle (TP-Link Nano / Mercusys / ASUS USB Adapter) and connect to the hotspot
printer.troubleshoot.s3Step3: USB cashier printer keeps printing as usual. LAN cashier printer stays dark until the router recovers.
printer.troubleshoot.s3Step4: Emergency Mode ON → all tickets route to cashier → staff hand-delivers
printer.troubleshoot.s4Title: OS print dialog opens for every print (staff has to press Enter)
printer.troubleshoot.s4Why: Current connection method is Browser Print. For silent printing, switch to QZ Tray (Windows) or RawBT (Android). See the "Which method should I pick?" table above for environment-specific recommendations.

settingsPage.whatIsQzTrayDesc: QZ Tray is a small program that runs in the background on your POS device. It acts as a bridge between your web browser (or installed desktop app) and your network printers. Without it, the browser cannot send print data directly to LAN printers.
settingsPage.whereToInstallDesc1: Install QZ Tray on your main POS device only — the PC or tablet where you process orders and payments. This device must be connected to the same network (router/WiFi) as your printers.
settingsPage.whereToInstallDesc2: Kitchen display tablets, customer displays, and other secondary devices do not need QZ Tray installed.
settingsPage.qzScenarioMigration: Existing LAN printers (migrating from another POS)
settingsPage.qzScenarioMigrationDesc: Your printers are already on the network with assigned IP addresses. Your existing LAN cables, IP setup, and Windows printer drivers all stay unchanged — you only need to install QZ Tray on the new POS device and tell Purple POS which printer to use.
settingsPage.qzScenarioFreshDesc: Installing network printers for the first time. You will physically connect the printers to your router, find their IP addresses, then install QZ Tray and link them to Purple POS.
settingsPage.qzMigStep1Title: Check if QZ Tray is already installed (install if needed)
settingsPage.qzMigStep1Desc: Some web-based POS systems also use QZ Tray, so it may already be installed. Look at the Windows system tray (bottom-right corner near the clock). If you see the QZ Tray icon, it is already running — skip to the next step. If not, download from qz.io and install on this Windows POS (Mac and Linux are also supported). Your existing LAN cables, printer IP addresses, and Windows drivers remain unchanged.
settingsPage.qzMigStep1AlreadyInstalledH: Already installed? You can skip the download and go to the next step.
settingsPage.qzMigStep2Title: Confirm your existing printer IP addresses
settingsPage.qzMigStep2Desc: Look up the IP for each printer from your previous POS settings, the router's connected-devices list, or the printer's network status page. The standard print port is 9100 (example: 192.168.1.100:9100).
settingsPage.qzMigStep3Title: Enter printer addresses in Purple POS
settingsPage.qzMigStep3Desc: Enter the IP:Port for each printer below, or select an existing Windows-registered printer from the dropdown. Run Test Print on each printer to verify, then click Save.
settingsPage.qzFreshStep1Desc: Connect each printer to the router with a LAN cable (recommended) or via WiFi. Make sure every printer is on the same network as the POS device.
settingsPage.qzFreshStep2Desc: Print a network status page directly from the printer (refer to the printer's manual for the button combination), or open the router's connected-devices list. The standard print port is 9100.
settingsPage.qzFreshStep3Desc: In the router's DHCP settings, reserve each printer's IP so it does not change after a reboot. Skip this only if the printer manual recommends DHCP-only.
settingsPage.qzFreshStep4Title: Install QZ Tray on the POS device
settingsPage.qzFreshStep4Desc: Download from qz.io and install on your main POS device only. Available for Windows, Mac, and Linux. QZ Tray runs automatically in the system tray after installation.
settingsPage.qzFreshStep5Title: Enter printer addresses in Purple POS
settingsPage.qzFreshStep5Desc: Enter IP:Port (example: 192.168.1.100:9100) for each printer below. Run Test Print on each printer to verify, then click Save.
settingsPage.qzCommonAllowBrowserDesc: The first time Purple POS connects, QZ Tray will ask for permission. Click "Allow" or "Remember this decision" so you are not asked again.

settingsPage.qzDesktopAppNoteDesc: The Purple POS desktop app uses the same QZ Tray bridge as the browser. You can install Purple POS to your desktop ("Install" button in the sidebar) and printing will keep working with the same settings.
settingsPage.qzDiagramFooter: Your existing LAN cables and network setup remain unchanged. QZ Tray simply enables the browser or desktop app to send print data through the same network.
